sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: Parallel lines, transversal, one angle 70°. Alternate interior angle?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 42° and 69°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 115°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 66. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 66, and it is parallel to the third side
33, and it is perpendicular to the third side
33, and it is parallel to the third side
132, and it is parallel to the third side

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: A proof concludes that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 77°. Find the measure of the corresponding angle.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 70° and 53°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
